system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID | Seller position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (**AUD 4.8m**). | 25% of price (**AUD 6m**). The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the draft; none is given. | **Reject; propose 25% / AUD 6m.** Do not use the unauthorised 20% fallback. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter at playbook thresholds.** The Seller’s thresholds are materially higher and its tipping-point treatment is less favourable. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller also proposes limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | 24 months for general claims; 18 months is available only with Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject; require 24 months and limit this period to general claims.** The proposed fallback lacks approval and risks bleeding into other claim regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; seek the separate playbook regime.** Title and capacity risks should not be confined to general-warranty limits. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; this cannot be waived. | **Insist on an express carve-out.** The Seller’s all-Claims wording could otherwise purport to restrict these claims. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Reject the general disclosures and require specific fair disclosure.** A blanket disclosure risks defeating warranties without identifying the relevant matters fairly. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions; if any qualifier remains, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the blanket exclusion.** Constructive knowledge of broad records is not an acceptable substitute for the agreed targeted approach. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. The letter says no final consent or evidence of condition satisfaction is included. | Effective consent **and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Require an effective, conditioned-and-satisfied consent before Completion.** Consent-on-delivery does not establish that the contractual conditions are met. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. The letter confirms no repayment or final security discharge is included. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require payout and release at Completion; do not accept a post-Completion release without both safeguards.** The facility and security remain outstanding on the disclosed facts. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 closing bonuses not separately itemised in the funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded, with no silent exclusion from the funds flow. | **Require the funds flow to address the bonuses and on-costs expressly.** The disclosed amounts are omitted and the potential additional costs are unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 open is not independently verified, and no payment receipt or assignment is in the data room. | Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; treat AUD 180,000 as unverified, not established either way. | **Broaden the indemnity and preserve the cure.** The disclosure does not establish payment or assignment, so neither a narrow indemnity nor a definitive payment assumption is justified. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed breach or loss is established. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Require preservation, investigation and updates without asserting a confirmed breach or quantified loss.** The disclosed record is preliminary and does not resolve access, scope or notification. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total AUD 330,000; Seller calls them ordinary-course operating costs. The letter does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Assess them on their actual terms and treatment; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Seek the underlying terms and assess; do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt.** The disclosure leaves key liability and timing facts open. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime; its proposed limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate, with no hidden override by the general regime; Tax/IP terms remain open. | **Reject the asserted settlement and preserve distinct regimes pending agreement.** The general limitations must not silently determine unresolved category-specific terms. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 share register showing Seller as holder of 100%; no independent proof is included. | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent verification. | **Require independent evidence and Buyer verification.** The register identifies the Seller’s source but does not itself complete the required verification. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime. | Leave Tax/IP terms open; do not assume unlimited liability or any resolution. | **Reject deemed settlement and negotiate these terms separately.** The playbook says they remain open and provides no basis to assume unlimited liability. |
=== END ADVICE ===
